settings.label: Subdomain
settings.meaning: The account the app talks to: acme for https://acme.zendesk.com.
settings.whereToFind: The first part of the account's address, https://<subdomain>.zendesk.com. Zendesk has no test keys: for test, use a sandbox (Enterprise plans: Admin Center › Account › Sandbox) or a trial account, each with its own subdomain and its own credentials.

settings.label: OAuth client identifier
settings.meaning: With the client secret, gets the server its access tokens to the Support API (OAuth client credentials). Requests act as the admin who made the client.
settings.whereToFind: Admin Center › Apps and integrations › APIs › OAuth clients › Add OAuth client, kind Confidential: the Identifier. Make it as a dedicated admin or agent if who did what matters in audits.

settings.label: OAuth client secret
settings.meaning: The confidential OAuth client's secret. Never sent to a browser.
settings.whereToFind: Admin Center › Apps and integrations › APIs › OAuth clients: the Secret, shown once when the client is saved.

settings.label: API token's agent email
settings.meaning: Only with an API token: the email address of the agent or admin the token signs in as.
settings.whereToFind: The email address of the agent whose API token ZENDESK_API_TOKEN is. API tokens are being retired (no new ones since October 27, 2026; all stop on April 30, 2027): use an OAuth client instead.

settings.label: API token (legacy)
settings.meaning: Only for an account that still has one: signs in to the Support API as ZENDESK_EMAIL. Used when no OAuth client is set.
settings.whereToFind: Admin Center › Apps and integrations › APIs › API tokens. Zendesk no longer issues new ones and turns the rest off on April 30, 2027.

settings.label: Web Widget key
settings.meaning: Which messaging Web Widget the app's pages load.
settings.whereToFind: Admin Center › Channels › Messaging and social › Messaging › your widget › Installation: the key= value in the snippet's address.

settings.label: Messaging signing key ID
settings.meaning: Names the signing key in the header (kid) of the JWT that signs a user in to the Web Widget.
settings.whereToFind: Admin Center › Account › Security › End user authentication › Messaging › Create key: the key's ID, listed on that tab (it looks like app_5963ceb97cde542d000dbdb1).

settings.label: Messaging signing key secret
settings.meaning: Signs (HS256) the JWT that tells the Web Widget who the user is, so nobody can claim to be someone else. Never sent to a browser.
settings.whereToFind: Admin Center › Account › Security › End user authentication › Messaging › Create key: the shared secret, shown in full only when the key is made.

settings.label: Webhook signing secret
settings.meaning: Checks that a webhook came from Zendesk. Each webhook has its own.
settings.whereToFind: Admin Center › Apps and integrations › Webhooks › Webhooks › your webhook › Reveal secret (or the Show Webhook Signing Secret API).

settings.label: Events source name
settings.meaning: The name trackEvent gives the app in a user's event timeline, and the source of the profiles it makes. app when unset; zendesk is reserved.
settings.whereToFind: A short name of your own, such as the app's name. Keep it stable: it is part of each user profile's identity.

operations.name: oauth.token
operations.purpose: Gets an access token for the Support API with the OAuth client's identifier and secret (grant_type client_credentials).

operations.name: users.createOrUpdate
operations.purpose: Creates a user, or updates the one with this external_id or email address. Answers 201 when it created one, 200 when it updated one.

operations.name: users.get
operations.purpose: Reads one user by Zendesk id.

operations.name: users.search
operations.purpose: Finds users by external_id, or by a query in Zendesk's search syntax, a page at a time.

operations.name: organizations.createOrUpdate
operations.purpose: Creates an organization, or updates the one with this external_id or id (never matched by name).

operations.name: tickets.create
operations.purpose: Creates a ticket with its first comment. The same Idempotency-Key and body within two hours gives back the same ticket.

operations.name: tickets.update
operations.purpose: Changes a ticket's status, priority, subject, tags or fields, optionally adding a comment.

operations.name: tickets.listRequested
operations.purpose: Lists the tickets a user requested, a page at a time (cursor pagination).

operations.name: tickets.search
operations.purpose: Finds tickets with Zendesk's search syntax (type:ticket is added), a page at a time.

operations.name: comments.list
operations.purpose: Lists a ticket's comments, oldest first, a page at a time (cursor pagination).

operations.name: comments.add
operations.purpose: Adds a public reply or an internal note to a ticket: a ticket update carrying only a comment.

operations.name: events.track
operations.purpose: Records an event in a user's timeline (the Events API), against a profile identified by the user's external_id. Answers 202.

signature.description: X-Zendesk-Webhook-Signature is the base64 HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the webhook's signing secret (its text, as shown), of the X-Zendesk-Webhook-Signature-Timestamp header's value (ISO 8601, such as 2021-03-25T05:09:27Z) followed by the raw request body. A delivery whose timestamp is more than five minutes from now is refused. Zendesk event deliveries are deduplicated on the body's id; trigger and automation deliveries, whose body the account writes, on the signature.

events.meaning: A comment was added to a ticket.
A ticket was assigned to another agent.
A user was merged into another.
